selected.name: Search beyond excluded activity for alternatives
selected.description: When a question asks what activity a person or group planned/did instead of a known activity, use this to avoid over-anchoring retrieval on the excluded activity.
content: If the user asks for an alternative, replacement, or activity done instead of a previously mentioned activity, do not build all searches and keywords around the excluded activity; the supporting memory may omit that activity entirely.

Run additional searches using the subject person/group plus substitution intent terms such as 'instead', 'alternative', 'planned to', and 'decided to', and search broadly for shared plans, preferences, or recent events involving the same people.

Before answering, inspect retrieved memories that mention plans or shared activities for those people even if they do not mention the excluded activity; select the memory that explicitly states the alternative plan rather than the first semantically similar result.

nearby_not_selected.name: Per-Entity Expansion for Intersection Queries
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a question asks what two or more entities share or have in common.
content: If the initial search for a multi-entity intersection query returns no overlap, do not repeat the identical query; issue separate searches for each entity using its name and known aliases.

After each per-entity search, collect concrete attribute values (cities, activities, preferences) from retrieved memories and issue follow-up searches combining each entity with those candidate values.
Conclude 'no information' only after per-entity searches for all entities and candidate-value expansions have been attempted and still yield no supporting memory.

nearby_not_selected.name: Per-person profile search for shared-interest questions
nearby_not_selected.description: When a question asks what interests, hobbies, or preferences two or more people share, search each person's profile/hobby memories separately before answering.
content: When the question asks what two or more named people share (interests, hobbies, preferences, or similar traits), run a separate profile/hobby search for each person (e.g., query with the person's name and 'hobbies' or 'interests') in addition to a joint-activity search.

Do not treat plans to do something together, one-time joint events, or supportive gestures as evidence of a shared interest; require either an explicit shared-interest memory or overlapping individual profile/preference memories.
After initial retrieval, judge evidence sufficiency for the comparison: if the evidence only describes activities done or planned together, run the per-person profile searches again before answering.

nearby_not_selected.name: Expand abstract positive-evaluative queries with concrete vocabulary
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a question asks what someone recently did that was rewarding, fulfilling, or a main stressor.
content: If the question uses abstract positive descriptors like 'rewarding experience', 'fulfilling', or 'sense of accomplishment' and the initial retrieval does not return an event memory that explicitly describes an achievement or positive outcome, run an additional keyword or structured search using concrete achievement verbs and nouns (e.g., 'presented', 'conference', 'received positive feedback', 'award', 'recognized').

Before answering a question about a person's main stressor, source of stress, or biggest difficulty, issue searches that go beyond the literal question wording: include stress-related synonyms (stressful, tough, difficult, hard, pressure, overwhelmed) and common life domains (work, family, school, health, finances, relationships).

If the question explicitly excludes a topic ('besides X', 'other than X', 'apart from X'), do not let that excluded topic dominate the query; run an additional search replacing the excluded topic with likely alternative domains.
Do not answer from an indirect memory that only implies the stressor through an overlap or trade-off; keep searching until a memory explicitly states what is stressful, tough, or difficult.

nearby_not_selected.name: Temporal-anchor post-milestone retrieval
nearby_not_selected.description: When a question asks what someone did or planned after a dated milestone event (e.g., after a wedding) and the first search results appear unrelated or pre-date the event.
content: When a question asks what someone did or plans to do after a dated milestone event, use the milestone date as a temporal anchor; run searches with typical follow-up activity terms (honeymoon, celebration, get-together, trip, activity) and filter or rank memories with world_start on or after that date.
If the first retrieval returns only memories dated before the milestone, do not answer from them; re-search with additional related terms and compare time windows.
Treat pre-milestone memories as non-evidence for post-milestone questions even when they share location or activity vocabulary.

nearby_not_selected.name: Expand retrieval for shared personal achievements
nearby_not_selected.description: When a question asks what achievement or news one person shared with another, retrieve events about either person alone and use a broader time window instead of requiring both names and exact date.
content: If a query describes an item 'shared with' or 'told to' another person, search for memories whose subject is either person individually; the sharing may be implicit and the memory may mention only the achiever.
Use a broadened time window (e.g., whole stated month or relative phrases like 'last week') rather than a single point date, so recent personal milestones are not excluded.
